'''Paul Mark Goldbart''' (born August 1960 in [[Chipping Barnet|Barnet]], [[Hertfordshire]], [[England]]) is an English-American physicist and author, and was the first director of the [[Institute for Condensed Matter Theory]] at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]]. His research ranges widely over the field of [[condensed matter physics]], including soft matter, disordered systems, nanoscience and [[superconductivity]]. Goldbart was provost of [[Stony Brook University]] from March 2021<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.stonybrook.edu/university/paul-m-goldbart-named-stony-brook-provost/|title=Paul M. Goldbart Named Stony Brook Provost|date=January 19, 2021}}</ref> until January 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Nassiri |first=Niki |last2=Lynders |first2=Maria |date=2022-01-23 |title=Paul Goldbart, executive vice president and provost, steps down |url=https://www.sbstatesman.com/2022/01/23/paul-goldbart-executive-vice-president-and-provost-steps-down/ |access-date=2022-08-03 |website=The Statesman |language=en-US}}</ref> Prior to that he had served as dean of the college of natural sciences at the [[University of Texas, Austin]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://news.utexas.edu/2018/04/12/paul-goldbart-named-dean-of-the-college-of-natural-sciences|title=Paul Goldbart Named Dean of the College of Natural Sciences|date=April 12, 2018}}</ref> Dean of the College of Sciences at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cos.gatech.edu/people |title=People {{!}} Georgia Tech College of Sciences |website=www.cos.gatech.edu |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719201936/http://www.cos.gatech.edu/people |archive-date=2011-07-19}}</ref> and as the director of the [[Institute for Condensed Matter Theory]].

==Career==
Goldbart earned his Ph.D. at [[Imperial College London]] in 1985 under Professor [[David Sherrington (physicist)|David Sherrington]]. Goldbart is a trustee of and the former [[Treasurer]]<ref>{{Deprecated archive|url=https://archive.today/20130414075329/http://www.aspenphys.org/aboutus/governance/officers.html|title=List of Officers}}</ref> for the [[Aspen Center for Physics]] in [[Colorado]].

He is a fellow of the [[Institute of Physics]] and the [[American Physical Society]].

==Books==
* M. Stone, P. Goldbart, "Mathematics for Physics: A guided Tour for Graduate Students" Cambridge University Press, 2009
* P. Goldbart, N. Goldenfeld, D. Sherrington, "Stealing the Gold: A Celebration of the Pioneering Physics of Sam Edwards (International Series of Monographs on Physics)" Oxford University Press, USA 2005
